final_candidates.decision_summary: C61 is a zinc-coordinating cysteine in the BRCA1 RING domain; glycine substitution abolishes zinc binding and E3 ligase activity with minimal steric perturbation, effectively eliminating tumor-suppressor function.

C64 is the second zinc-coordinating cysteine in the RING domain; glycine substitution disrupts zinc coordination and E3 ligase function while preserving overall protein folding due to the small side chain.

Arginine at position 61 disrupts zinc coordination via a large charged side chain, abolishing RING domain function; slightly lower confidence than glycine due to potential minor steric clashes but still highly effective at eliminating tumor-suppressor activity.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidates are well-supported by domain knowledge of BRCA1 RING domain zinc coordination; no external tools available to further refine.

history.rationale: C61 is a zinc-coordinating residue in the RING domain; mutation to glycine disrupts zinc binding and abolishes E3 ligase activity critical for BRCA1 tumor-suppressor function.

C61 is one of the zinc-coordinating cysteines in the RING domain; substitution to glycine abolishes zinc binding and E3 ligase activity while the small side chain minimizes steric disruption to local backbone.
C64 is another zinc-coordinating cysteine in the RING domain; substitution with glycine disrupts the zinc-binding motif and impairs BRCA1-BARD1 interaction and E3 ligase activity.

C64 is the second zinc-coordinating cysteine in the RING domain; glycine substitution disrupts zinc coordination and E3 ligase function with minimal structural perturbation beyond the metal-binding site.
Substituting the zinc-coordinating C61 with arginine disrupts RING domain integrity and E3 ligase activity while likely preserving overall protein folding.

Arginine at position 61 introduces a large charged residue that disrupts zinc coordination and may cause local unfolding of the RING domain, but the bulky side chain could introduce minor steric clashes.
C64 is a zinc-coordinating residue in the RING domain; arginine substitution disrupts zinc binding and impairs tumor-suppressor function.
Similar logic to C61R; arginine disrupts zinc coordination at the second cysteine but the large side chain may cause slightly more local distortion than glycine.
Alanine substitution at zinc-coordinating C61 disrupts RING domain zinc binding without introducing steric clashes, preserving overall fold.

Alanine removes the zinc-coordinating thiol with minimal steric impact, but the methyl group is slightly larger than hydrogen, making it marginally less disruptive than glycine for abolishing function.
Alanine substitution at C64 removes the zinc-coordinating thiol, disrupting RING domain integrity while maintaining overall protein stability.
Same rationale as C61A but at the second zinc-coordinating cysteine; slightly lower confidence due to potential differences in local structural context.

Serine is a conservative substitution for cysteine (isosteric hydroxyl for thiol) that abolishes zinc coordination; known pathogenic variant in BRCA1 RING domain. Preserves local structure well but may retain partial metal binding.
Serine at position 64 abolishes zinc coordination with minimal structural perturbation; conservative substitution that preserves backbone geometry while eliminating the critical thiol.
